stem: A 9-year-old child has a clearly localised soft tissue infection, is alert, well perfused, and not tachycardic; which investigation strategy is most appropriate?

options.text: Full sepsis workup for every child with fever and a bacterial focus
Blood culture in all cases regardless of age or appearance
Lumbar puncture because a focal infection can still hide sepsis
Investigations specific to the definite focus unless the child becomes toxic
No investigations are ever needed when a focus is identified

explanation: Investigations specific to the definite focus are most appropriate here. In a well older child with a clear localised infection and no toxic features, broader sepsis investigations are not the default unless the child becomes toxic.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: A definite focus narrows the investigation approach in a well child. Broader sepsis assessment is reserved for children with concerning features such as toxicity.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a full sepsis workup is not recommended for every child with a localised infection.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because blood cultures are not mandatory in all children with a definite focus; the need depends on the clinical picture.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because lumbar puncture is not indicated for a well child with an isolated soft tissue focus and no neurological or toxic features.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because a child with a definite focus of infection should have investigations directed to that focus unless they become toxic.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a focus does not rule out the need for investigations; tests should be targeted to the identified source.
